kid: When I unlock the door, I do the opposite of locking it.
notes: #1 prefix: 26% of prefixed words (White et al. 1989). Anglo-Saxon, not Latin/Greek, but too important to skip.

kid: If I reread a book, I read it again.
Something impossible is not possible.
notes: #3 prefix (11%). Spelling changes before the next letter: im- before b/m/p, il- before l, ir- before r.

kid: When the magician's rabbit disappears, it does the opposite of appear.
notes: #4 prefix (7%). With un-, re-, in-, covers about 58% of prefixed words.

kid: To enlarge a photo is to cause it to be large.
A nonstop flight does not stop until it lands.
When you import toys, you carry them into the country.
notes: #7 prefix (3.5%). Same spelling as in- 'not'; context tells which.

kid: If you overeat at a party, you eat too much.
If you misspell a word, you spell it wrongly.
A submarine travels under the water.
We preheat the oven before we bake cookies.
An intersection is where two roads meet between corners.
A weather forecast tells you the weather before it happens.
We defrost frozen peas to undo the freezing.
Robots that transform change across from car to robot.
A superhero has powers above a normal person's.
notes: #16 prefix (1.5%). sur- is its French form (surface, survive).

kid: A semicircle is half of a circle.
Antifreeze works against freezing in a car.
Midnight is the middle of the night.
Fish live underwater, below the surface.
When you connect blocks, you join them together.
notes: Top prefix in academic words (Lane et al. 2019), though not in White's list because it usually attaches to bound roots.

kid: When you exhale, you breathe air out.
notes: High-frequency in academic words (Lane et al. 2019).

kid: A propeller pushes a boat forward.
notes: High-frequency in academic words (Lane et al. 2019).

kid: A magnet attracts metal, pulling it toward itself.
notes: Top-4 prefix in academic words (Lane et al. 2019). Usually 'hides' by changing its last letter to match the root (ad+tract = attract).

kid: A perfect score is complete all the way through.
notes: In Lane et al. 2019 academic list.

kid: If you are absent, you are away from school.
notes: In Lane et al. 2019 academic list.

kid: An obstacle is something in the way.
notes: In Lane et al. 2019 academic list.

kid: If the game is postponed, it happens after the planned time.
An autograph is a name a star writes by herself.
A telescope lets you see stars far away.
A microscope helps you see very small things.
A multicolor rainbow has many colors.
A unicorn has one horn.
A bicycle has two wheels.
A triangle has three sides.
A monorail train runs on one rail.
A polygon is a shape with many sides.
The circumference is the distance around a circle.
To contradict someone is to speak against what they said.
An extraterrestrial comes from beyond Earth.
When you introduce a friend, you bring them inside the group.
A malfunction is when a machine works badly.
A benefit is something good you get.
A symphony is many instruments sounding together.
notes: High-frequency Greek element in ELA (Lane et al. 2019).

kid: A diagonal line goes across a square from corner to corner.
Parallel lines run beside each other and never meet.
The perimeter is the distance around a shape.
An epilogue is an extra part added on at the end of a story.
A hyperactive puppy has too much energy.
Hypothermia means your body heat drops below normal.
Anonymous means without a name.
notes: Greek 'alpha privative'; hard to spot, best taught late.

kid: A panorama picture shows all the view at once.
An omnivore eats all kinds of food, plants and meat.
The equator splits Earth into two equal halves.
A kilometer is one thousand meters.
A millipede looks like it has a thousand legs.
A century is one hundred years.

meaning: act or result of (makes a noun)
kid: An invention is the result of inventing something new.
notes: Top derivational suffix (-tion/-ation/-ition = 4% of all suffixed words; White et al. 1989).

kid: A washable shirt can be washed.
A musical show is related to music.
notes: #1 suffix in academic words (Lane et al. 2019).

kid: A rainy day is full of rain.
Kindness is the state of being kind.
If you walk quietly, you walk in a quiet way.
A sailor is a person who sails.
notes: -er is Anglo-Saxon; -or is Latin (actor, inventor). 4% of suffixed words.

kid: Electricity is the quality of being electric.
Excitement is the feeling that comes from being excited.
A heroic act is like something a hero would do.
A dangerous road is full of danger.
When you sharpen a pencil, you make it sharp.

meaning: tending to; having the quality of
kid: A creative kid tends to create new things.
A helpful friend is full of help.
A fearless kid is without fear.
The tallest giraffe is the most tall.
notes: Comparative -er and superlative -est together (White ranks both in top 20). Anglo-Saxon.

kid: A pianist is a person who plays the piano.
Heroism is the act of being a hero.
To memorize is to make something stay in your memory.
Zoology is the study of animals.
Silence is the state of being silent.
A servant is one who serves.
A library is a place for books.
To activate a toy is to make it active.
A mixture is the result of mixing things.
A magnifying glass makes things look bigger.
A magician is a person who does magic.
Storage is a place to store things.
Greenish paint is somewhat green.
Friendship is the state of being friends.
Childhood is the time of being a child.
A solar panel is related to the sun.
In a democracy, the people rule by voting.
Arachnophobia is a fear of spiders.
notes: Low frequency but highly memorable for kids.

kid: A portable speaker is easy to carry.
notes: porta/portus 'gate/harbor' (airport, opportunity) is a close relative.

kid: A spectator looks at the game from the stands.
notes: Note: special/species/spice share the root (specere) but meaning drifted; excluded from counts.

kid: To predict is to say what will happen before it happens.
An autograph is a name someone writes by hand.
Builders construct a house by putting it together.
A projector throws a picture onto the wall.
When you scribble, you write in a messy way.
A train conductor leads the train.
A factory is a place where things are made.
notes: Very productive: -fect, -fic, -fy all come from facere.

kid: When you capture a bug, you take it and hold it.
A missile is something sent flying through the air.
To deposit money is to put it in the bank.
notes: Top Latin root in academic words (Lane et al. 2019).

kid: A statue stands still in the park.
notes: #2 Latin root in academic words (Lane et al. 2019).

kid: A video is something you can see.
A tractor pulls heavy things on a farm.
When a volcano erupts, it breaks open.
A uniform gives everyone the same shape and look.
An audience is the people who hear the show.
An event is something that comes and happens.
To reverse is to turn back the other way.
A motor makes a car move.
A ferry carries cars across the water.
When you press a button, you push it.
A magnet can repel another magnet, pushing it away.
To extend your arm is to stretch it out.
A container holds things inside it.
A river current is water that runs fast.
When you graduate, you step up to the next level.
A sequel is a movie that follows the first one.
To select a snack is to choose one.
Dialogue is words spoken between characters.
notes: #1 Greek root in academic words (Lane et al. 2019).

kid: Biology is the study of life.
Geography is about places on Earth.
A photograph is a picture made with light.
Headphones bring sound to your ears.
A thermometer measures how hot something is.
A speedometer measures how fast a car goes.
notes: measure/dimension come from the related Latin metiri.

kid: A periscope lets a submarine look above the water.
A fire hydrant gives firefighters water.
An astronaut travels toward the stars.
Chronological order puts events in time order.
A bicycle has two wheels.
Empathy means feeling what someone else feels.
notes: Not 'path' as in trail (that's Old English).

kid: Philadelphia's name means 'city of brotherly love.'
Technology uses skill and science to build tools.
A psychologist helps people understand their minds.
A generator produces electricity.
A native plant was born and grew in that place.
Vitamins help your body stay alive and healthy.
An immortal hero in a myth never dies.
A manual can opener works by hand.
You push a bike pedal with your foot.
notes: Greek pod 'foot' (tripod, podium) is a cousin.

kid: An incredible story is hard to believe.
A judge decides what is right in court.
The location is the place where something is.
Marine animals live in the sea.
A terrarium is a little container of earth and plants.
notes: terrible/terrify come from a different root (terrere 'frighten').

kid: An aquarium is a water tank for fish.
Solar panels use energy from the sun.
notes: Two roots share this spelling: sol 'sun' and solus 'alone'.

kid: Your signature is the special mark of your name.
A pronoun stands for a person's name.
A vocal song uses your voice.
To verify a fact is to check that it is true.
A laboratory is a place where scientists work.
The Statue of Liberty stands for being free.
A memory is something your mind keeps.
A sensor feels changes like heat or light.
A scientist works to know how the world works.
A pendulum hangs and swings back and forth.
To multiply is to fold a number over many times.
The final round is the end of the game.
A mirror reflects light, bending it back.
A fluid is something that flows, like water.
A fragile vase can break easily.
A junction is where two roads join.
To include a friend is to close them into the group.
Scissors cut paper.
A procession is a line of people going forward.
A president sits at the head of a country's government.
Ordinal numbers tell the order: first, second, third.
When we cooperate, we work together.
A commander gives orders.
Birds migrate, moving south for the winter.
A novice is someone new at something.
A numeral is a symbol for a number.
The population is all the people in a place.
Primary colors are the first colors you mix others from.
A question is how you ask for something you want to know.
A rectangle has four straight sides and right angles.
Earth rotates, turning once every day.
To conserve water is to save it.
Similar shapes look alike.
A supersonic jet is faster than sound.
When you perspire, your skin 'breathes' out sweat.
Contact means to touch or reach someone.
A temporary tattoo lasts only a short time.
A suburb is the area just outside a city.
A vacuum sucks the air out until a space is empty.
A valuable coin is worth a lot of money.
The Earth revolves, rolling around the Sun.
A voyage is a trip along a long way.
A victory is when you conquer and win.
A zoo is a place to see animals.
An anniversary comes once every year.
A minibus is a small bus.
A magnifying glass makes things look large.
A megaphone makes your voice huge.
A patriot loves their fatherland, their country.
Maternity clothes are for moms-to-be.
A fortress is a strong building that protects people.
The captain is the head of the team.
A corporation is a group that acts as one body.
A dentist takes care of your teeth.
A dormant volcano is 'sleeping' and not erupting.
A habitat is where an animal lives.
A luminous watch glows with light.
The median strip is in the middle of the road.
When you admire a painting, you look at it with wonder.
A monument shows us someone to remember.
To navigate is to steer a ship or find your way.
notes: naut is the Greek cousin (astronaut = star sailor).

kid: The Pacific Ocean was named for its peaceful waters.
A portion is a part of the whole meal.
A picture is a painting or photo of something.
If something is possible, you are able to do it.
An escalator helps you climb stairs without walking.
An insect's body is 'cut' into sections.
A social person likes being with a group.
Sugar dissolves in water, loosening into tiny bits.
To contribute is to give your share.
A useful tool is easy to use.
A democracy is ruled by the people.
Dynamite has powerful explosive force.
An ecosystem is the 'home' where plants and animals live together.
An electrician fixes things that use electricity.
Cinema means moving pictures.
A mechanic fixes machines like cars.
A caterpillar's metamorphosis changes its whole shape.
Physical exercise is good for your body.
Police keep a city safe.
A sphere is shaped like a ball.
A monochrome picture uses only one color.
Homophones sound the same but are spelled differently.
Dinosaur means 'terrible lizard.'
notes: Very low word count but a strong hook for young kids.

kid: Anthropology is the study of humans.
A bibliography is a list of books you used.
An optician makes glasses for your eyes.
